Hi Hannah,

Quick note from procurement at Quell — our legal and finance teams reviewed the latest private offer and asked whether we can do a staged activation for the new capacity rather than all at once. Their ask is: commit to the 18-month term but roll the additional capacity in two tranches tied to usage thresholds (50% activation at 60% of baseline, full activation at 130% of baseline). They also asked about invoice timing (monthly vs. quarterly) and whether we can bridge capacity in months where usage spikes.

Could you point me to the right person on Redwood's side to confirm logistics (marketplace paperwork, invoicing cadence, and any PO amendment language)? We want to keep the private offer but avoid a large upfront invoice.

Thanks,
Samantha Liu

Looping in ops and marketplace leads. Hi all — I reviewed Quell's SOW. Operational notes:

- Marketplace private-offer paperwork: AWS Private Offer form can support staged activations but we must list the capacity tiers and the transfer schedule in the PO amendment. I've attached a draft AWS_Private_Offer_Form.pdf with the fields prefilled for Quell.
- Invoice cadence: we can do monthly invoices tied to actual usage with a staged commitment invoice at the start of each tranche (smaller amounts). Alternatively, Quell can accept quarterly invoicing — both are supported; monthly keeps cash-flow aligned with usage.
- Bridge policy: we can implement a temporary bridge pool (30 days credit) that covers spikes beyond the current tranche while the next tranche is pending, billed at the same unit rate and reconciled on the next invoice.

I'll prepare a sample invoice layout reflecting staged activation (attached Staged_Activation_Timeline.xlsx) and propose the exact wording for the PO amendment. Rafael — can you draft contract language that references the activation thresholds and the temporary bridge clause?

Thanks Marissa — drafting language now. Draft highlights for the PO amendment:

1) Staged Activation: Quell commits to the total annualized capacity described in SOW v3. Activation happens in two tranches: Tranche A (50% of additional capacity) becomes effective when 60% of baseline utilization is exceeded for two consecutive billing cycles; Tranche B (remaining 50%) becomes effective when 130% of baseline utilization is exceeded for one billing cycle.

2) Bridge Capacity: For months where usage exceeds the currently active tranche, Redwood will auto-provision a short-term bridge equal to up to 20% of total committed capacity for a period not exceeding 30 days. Charges for bridge capacity will be invoiced on the next invoice and reconciled in the following billing period.

3) Invoice Timing: Default to monthly invoicing unless Quell requests quarterly; monthly invoices will include line items for staged-tranche commitments, actual usage charges, and any bridge reconciliation.

4) Marketplace Execution: Marissa to confirm exact AWS Private Offer field values; once Quell signs the amendment we will push the private offer through AWS and schedule a staged activation window.

I'll attach a tracked-change version of the PO amendment once I have final baseline numbers.

-Rafael
Senior Counsel, Commercial
Redwood Inference
